questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between a sequence and its corresponding series?

options.text: A sequence is an ordered list of terms, while a series is the sum of the terms of a sequence.
A sequence is the sum of terms, while a series is an ordered list of numbers.
options.why: Reversed the definitions of sequence and series.

options.text: A sequence and a series are identical mathematical objects with different names.
options.why: Treated an ordered list and a sum as the same mathematical concept.

options.text: A sequence is always finite, whereas a series is always infinite.
options.why: Confused the list/sum distinction with the finite/infinite distinction.

questions.solution_text: A sequence is an ordered list of terms, whereas a series is the addition of the terms of a sequence.

questions.question_text: For the sequence $6, 11, 16, 21, 26, 31, \dots$, what is the value of the partial sum $S_{4}$?

options.why: Gave the 4th term $a_{4}$ instead of the partial sum $S_{4}$.
Added five terms ($S_{5}$) instead of four terms ($S_{4}$).
Multiplied the 4th term by 4 or made an addition error.

questions.question_text:
A sequence is given by $a_{n} = 3n - 1$.
What is the value of the partial sum $S_{3}$?

options.why: Gave the 3rd term $a_{3}$ instead of the sum of the first three terms.
Calculated $3 \times a_{3} = 3 \times 6$ or made an arithmetic error.
Added four terms including $a_{4} = 11$.

questions.question_text:
The partial sums of a sequence are $S_{4} = 50$ and $S_{5} = 72$.
What is the value of the 5th term, $a_{5}$?

options.why: Added $S_{5} + S_{4}$ instead of subtracting $S_{5} - S_{4}$.
Gave the partial sum $S_{5}$ instead of the individual term $a_{5}$.
Divided $S_{5}$ by 5 instead of computing $S_{5} - S_{4}$.

questions.question_text: For a sequence with partial sum formula $S_{n}$, which expression represents the sum of the terms $a_{4} + a_{5} + a_{6} + a_{7}$?

options.why: Subtracted $S_{4}$, which wrongly removes $a_{4}$ from the required sum.
Counted the four terms as ending at $a_{8}$ by adding $4$ to the starting index $4$.
Made both index slips: ended at $S_{8}$ and also removed $a_{4}$ by subtracting $S_{4}$.

questions.question_text:
The partial sum of a sequence is given by $S_{n} = 2n^{2} + 3n$.
What is the value of the 4th term, $a_{4}$?

options.why: Evaluated $S_{4}$ instead of $a_{4} = S_{4} - S_{3}$.
Evaluated $2(4) + 3$ instead of computing $S_{4} - S_{3}$.
Added $S_{4} + S_{3} = 44 + 27$ instead of subtracting.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has partial sums $S_{3} = 18$ and $S_{7} = 98$.
What is the value of $a_{4} + a_{5} + a_{6} + a_{7}$?

options.why: Added $S_{7} + S_{3} = 98 + 18$ instead of finding the difference.
Gave $S_{7}$ without subtracting $S_{3}$.
Divided the difference 80 by 4 terms.

questions.question_text:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of a sequence is $S_{n} = 3n^{2} - n$.
What is the formula for the $n$th term $a_{n}$ for $n \ge 2$?

options.why: Differentiated $S_{n}$ with respect to $n$ instead of computing $S_{n} - S_{n-1}$.
Divided $S_{n}$ by $n$ instead of computing $S_{n} - S_{n-1}$.
Expanded $3(n-1)^{2} - (n-1)$ with sign errors in the constant term.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has partial sum formula $S_{n} = 4n^{2} + 2n$.
What is the formula for the $n$th term $a_{n}$ for $n \ge 2$?

options.why: Differentiated $S_{n}$ with respect to $n$ instead of computing $S_{n} - S_{n-1}$.
Divided $S_{n}$ by $n$ instead of using $a_{n} = S_{n} - S_{n-1}$.
Made a sign error when subtracting the constant term in $S_{n-1}$.
The difference isolates the newly added twentieth term, not the first partial sum.
Uses the first term instead of the term added when forming $S_{20}$.
The nineteenth term was already included in both partial sums and cancels.
